matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: Before moving any stick, compute the numeric values of both sides (including any addition or subtraction) to find the numeric imbalance; then consider single‑stick transformations that change a side by exactly that amount (e.g., ±1, ±2, ±5).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Use whenever the equation is false and you need to decide which stick move could correct it.
matchstick.example: Attempting a stick move without first checking that the left side exceeds the right side by 14, leading to a transformation that cannot possibly balance the equation.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the side that must increase is short by exactly 5 and a V appears there, add a diagonal stick to the V (taken from elsewhere) to turn it into an X, raising its value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance is 5 and a V is present on the side that needs to grow.
matchstick.example: Leaving a V unchanged when the imbalance is exactly 5, missing the opportunity to turn it into an X and add 5.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral that already contains at least one I to another numeral that can legally accept an extra I (e.g., turning V into VI or appending an I), thereby adjusting the values by ±1 on each side.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is 2 (or 1) and moving an I between numerals can correct it.
matchstick.example: Removing an I from a numeral that would become invalid (e.g., turning a solitary I into nothing).

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If both a minus sign (single horizontal) and an equals sign (two horizontals) appear, you can relocate one horizontal from the equals sign to the minus sign, turning the minus into an equals and the original equals into a minus; both remain valid operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both '-' and '=', and the numeric imbalance suggests that swapping them could help.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from '=' but forgetting to also change the original '-' to '=', resulting in two minus signs.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the side that must decrease is short by exactly 5 and an X appears there, remove one diagonal stick from the X (and optionally reposition it elsewhere) to turn it into a V, lowering its value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance is 5 and an X is present on the side that needs to shrink.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X and discarding it, leaving a single diagonal that is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Evaluate expressions when computing numeric imbalance
matchstick.principle: Fully evaluate any arithmetic on each side (including addition and subtraction) before comparing numeric values; treat the result as a single number for each side.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving any matchstick equation, before considering stick moves.
matchstick.example: Comparing the raw numerals 'XVI' and 'XV' without performing the subtraction, miscalculating the imbalance.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick across equality
matchstick.principle: When the numeric imbalance is exactly 2, you can move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral on the side with excess to a numeral on the opposite side, decreasing the larger side by 1 and increasing the smaller side by 1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Imbalance 2 and both sides contain numerals that can lose/gain an I without becoming invalid.
matchstick.example: Moving an I from a numeral on one side to the other side when the source numeral would become invalid (e.g., turning 'I' into an empty symbol).

matchstick.title: Reposition I before X to change XI to IX
matchstick.principle: If a numeral contains the pattern 'XI', moving its I‑stick to the left of the X changes the numeral to 'IX', decreasing its value by 2.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is 2 and a 'XI' appears on the side that must decrease.
matchstick.example: Moving the I from 'XI' to elsewhere, losing the chance to form 'IX' and adjust by 2.

matchstick.title: Convert '+' to '-' by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: If a plus sign is present, moving its vertical stick to a numeral adds an I (increase by 1) and simultaneously turns the plus into a minus, adjusting the arithmetic accordingly.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is 1 and a plus sign is present on the side that must increase.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' but not updating the plus to a minus, leaving an invalid '+' sign.

matchstick.title: Maintain operator validity when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: When relocating a stick from the equality sign, ensure that the remaining symbol still forms a valid operator (either keep both horizontals for '=', or leave a single horizontal to become '-', which is also valid). Without this, you may produce an invalid operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any transformation that takes a stick from '=', to avoid leaving an unrecognizable symbol.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal from '=' and treating the leftover single line as if it were still '=', resulting in an invalid equality sign.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any numeral can donate a stick, ignoring the structural constraints of Roman numerals.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Before moving a stick, verify that the source numeral will remain a valid Roman numeral after losing the stick.

matchstick.description: Providing an invalid equation after moving a stick (including incomplete or unreachable solutions)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on moving sticks but neglects to ensure the resulting symbols form a syntactically correct equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, check that every character is a recognized numeral or operator and that the equation format is preserved.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign and leaving no valid '=' sign in the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats the equality sign as immutable, not considering that removing a horizontal can produce a minus sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: If you remove a stick from '=', ensure the remaining symbol is a valid operator (either '=' or '-').

matchstick.description: Not verifying numeric equality after transformation; resulting equation may be syntactically valid but numerically false
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model stops after producing a syntactically correct equation, forgetting to evaluate its truth.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the numeric values of both sides after the move and confirm they match.

matchstick.description: Moving more than one stick (or removing multiple sticks) violates the single‑stick rule
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes attempts to change multiple symbols simultaneously, conflating multiple moves.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Restrict the transformation to a single stick relocation; any change to a symbol must be accounted for by moving exactly one stick.
